groups.title: Performance Optimization Theory
groups.question: Your recipe index page is slow: it runs hundreds of queries, renders the same partials on every request and filters on unindexed columns. Explain how you would fix each.

followUps.N+1 queries and eager loading with inclu: What is an N+1 query and how does includes fix it?
followUps.Fragment and Russian doll caching strate: How does Russian doll caching know when to expire?
followUps.Database indexing for query performance: Which columns should you index and how do you check the effect?

evidence.text: Loading an association inside a loop runs one query per record.
includes, preload or eager_load load associations up front.
This turns many queries into one or two.
Fragment caching stores rendered partials in a cache.
Cache keys include the record's updated time, so changes create a new key.
Nested caches expire the parent when a child changes, by touching the parent.
Index foreign keys and columns used for filtering and sorting.
Indexes are added in migrations.
EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows whether the query uses the index.

notEnough: Only saying indexes make queries faster.

groups.title: Code Architecture Patterns
groups.question: Your Order model has grown to 800 lines and controllers contain checkout logic. Explain how you would reorganise the code.

followUps.Service objects for complex business log: What is a service object and when should you use one?
followUps.Concerns and modules for code reuse: When is a concern a good fit, and when does it hide problems?

evidence.text: A service object is a plain Ruby class that does one business operation.
It keeps controllers thin and models focused on data.
It can be tested on its own without HTTP.
Concerns extract behaviour shared by several models or controllers.
They are modules that can define callbacks, scopes and methods.
Moving code into concerns without a real shared purpose just hides a large class.

groups.title: Caching Infrastructure
groups.question: You run several app servers and the cache is not shared, and browsers re-download pages that have not changed. Explain how you would configure caching.

followUps.Redis cache store configuration in Rails: Why use Redis as the cache store with several servers?
followUps.HTTP caching with ETags and Last-Modifie: How do ETags reduce work for unchanged pages?

evidence.text: A Redis cache is shared by every app server.
Entries can expire automatically.
An in-memory cache is per process, so servers would each hold different copies.
Rails can set ETag and Last-Modified headers on responses.
Browsers send them back on the next request.
If nothing changed, Rails replies 304 without rendering the body.

groups.title: Monitoring and Profiling Tools
groups.question: Some production requests are slow and you do not know why, and you want to see query counts while developing. Explain the monitoring and profiling tools you would use.

followUps.Application performance monitoring with: What does an APM tool like Scout show you?
followUps.rack-mini-profiler for request-level pro: What does rack-mini-profiler show while developing?

evidence.text: It traces slow requests in production.
It shows time spent in the database, views and code.
It flags issues like N+1 queries and memory growth.
It adds a badge on each page with timing information.
It shows how many SQL queries ran and how long they took.
It can show memory allocations to find heavy code.
